tasks.spec:
You are a code worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory; NEVER create or edit anything under /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself (an earlier worker wrongly wrote there; do not repeat that). Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git. Write short notes to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/astra-pipeline-eval-cases-notes/notes.md (create the directory).

OWNED FILES (new): bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json, tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py. Edit nothing else (the loader bench/pipeline_eval/model.py already exists: read it first and use its EvalCase / Expectation / load_cases exactly as written; if the JSON shape you need differs from what load_cases accepts, adapt the JSON, never the loader). No production code, no story data, no network, no model calls.

CONTEXT: Phase 3 of .plans/astra-implementation-plan.md (read its Phase 3 list) and the test list in .plans/astra-arch-review.md ('The test set should include'). The harness scores reference, action, state, prose, false reveal, unauthorized creation, forced progress and clarification separately. We now need the CASE FIXTURE for the continuity-initiative story only (no second story package; that is a recorded decision). Fixtures are built on the DRAWER-TO-TRUCK sequence in scene 1A: Kristin searches Michelle's workstation drawer, finds the memory card taped beneath it, pockets it, goes out to the truck, boards it (driver's seat, laptop on the passenger seat) and may drive off. Learn the real entity names, fact ids and reveal ids from data/stories/continuity-initiative (world.yaml, knowledge.yaml, handoffs.yaml, plot.md) and from tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py, tests/test_seating.py, tests/test_world_seats.py, tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py. Use ONLY ids and names that exist there; do not invent entities.

WRITE bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json: a JSON object {"cases":[...]} with at least one DIAGNOSTIC case and at least one HELD_OUT case (different wording and, where possible, a different start state) for EACH of these 13 categories (use exactly these category strings):
 short_reference_after_cue; same_phrase_two_referents; pocket_vs_withdraw; enter_vs_drive; ordered_compound; correction; harmless_vs_plot_bypassing_object; unresolved_existing_npc; refused_move_prose; concealment_then_npc; save_load_between_cue_and_followup; reveal_before_after_prerequisites; player_caused_dependency_damage.
Plus one category clarification_invariance (diagnostic and held_out): an ambiguous command after which an arm that asks a clarification must leave turn counter, fired/active pressure events unchanged (Expectation.clarification=true, clarification_leaves_clock_unchanged=true).
Each case: unique id (category-d1, category-h1, ...), a short comment-free field set matching the loader, scene '1A' (or another existing scene id where the category needs it, e.g. NPC encounter), setup_facts that really exist, commands, expect with only the metrics that case honestly checks. Expectations must describe the CORRECT behaviour per the PRD and arch review (for example the 'Put the card in my pocket.' after finding it expects state placing the card with Kristin and prose that does not say Kristin takes the card out; a refused move expects prose that shows refusal; the unresolved existing NPC case expects creation 'none'; the harmless-object case expects creation up to 'descriptive'; the plot-bypassing case expects creation 'none'). Do not weaken expectations to make a stub pass: no arm is run in this task.
PLAYER INPUT RULES (docs/player-input-guide.md, read it): imperative commands, never first-person narration ('Search the gap beneath the drawer.', not 'I search...'); possessives 'my pocket', 'my laptop'; no 'do not' / 'without' / 'avoid' restraint clauses; verb with a direct object; no non-events like 'Wait.'. Held-out commands must share NO exact command string with any diagnostic case, and must use different wording, not just a changed noun.

WRITE tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py (hermetic): load_cases on the file succeeds; every one of the 14 categories has >=1 diagnostic and >=1 held_out case; no command string appears in both splits; every setup_fact exists as a fact id in the real package (find how facts are declared: knowledge 'establishes' fact_ids and world/state facts; assert against the real loaded package from storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package(Path('data/stories/continuity-initiative'))); every scene id exists; every command passes a player-input check (does not start with 'I ' or 'I\'ll', contains none of ' do not ', ' without ', ' avoid ', is not 'Wait.'); every expectation that names required_reveals/allowed_reveals names a real knowledge id; every case with save_load_after has an index inside its commands; clarification_invariance cases set both clarification flags; ids unique.

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame, bench; print(storygame.__file__, bench.__file__)"` prints paths inside the cwd. Test: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py tests/test_pipeline_eval.py. CLI: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m bench.pipeline_eval report --cases bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json. Ruff on the test file: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py and -m ruff format on it. Do not use uv. In notes.md list the ids you used per case and any category you could not ground (and why). Reply with the files changed.
